params.body:
## Why

The Observatory's proposals include brands writing about themselves. Among the publishers queued because a post cited them are Amazon's European newsroom, Apple Newsroom and Arc'teryx, and the source list of 20 October holds 53 industry associations. Nothing on a proposal said so. Gentells Standard 0.18.0 adds `Source.perspective`: `independent`, `interested` or `self`.

## The change

- **`core/source-perspective.mjs`** stores a rating with one sentence why, who rated it (`engine` or the person's address) and when.
  - A competitor from the Standard's list is `interested` without asking a model.
  - Everything else is rated in batches of 25 on the scout's model (`discover` phase, Haiku 5.5 by default).
  - A batch that fails leaves its sources unrated for the next round.
  - Admitted sources and ratings a person made are left alone.
  - The rating refuses nothing, admits nothing and weighs nothing.
- **The scout** (`discover.mjs`):
  - It gives a rating with each source it proposes, in the same answer.
  - Every run ends by rating up to 50 unrated proposed or trial sources, whatever door they came in by: the source list, the publishers posts cite, or the academic follow-up.
  - `node packages/pipeline/discover.mjs perspective --limit N` rates more at once.
- **`POST /sources/:id/perspective`**: a team member changes the rating, with name and time. `/store/patch` refuses these fields, and a member of gentells.com can't reach the route.
- **The sources list** carries `perspective`, `perspectiveWhy`, `perspectiveBy` and `perspectiveAt`.
- **The pin** moves to Standard v0.18.0.

## The backlog

1,044 proposed and 25 trial sources have no rating yet. At 50 per scout run they're rated within a few days. To do it at once, after deploy:

```
node packages/pipeline/discover.mjs perspective --limit 1100
```

That is about 42 calls on the scout's model.

## A check on real proposals

I put 43 of today's real proposals through this prompt once, on Haiku 5.5.

- `self`: Apple Newsroom, Amazon's European newsroom, Arc'teryx, Epic Games Newsroom, Airbnb Newsroom, ASOS.
- `interested`: industry associations (Bitkom, ACEA, Comeos, Belgian Brewers), consultancies (Accenture, McKinsey with BoF), advocacy groups (5Rights) and marketplaces on their own users (2dehands, Amazon Movers & Shakers).
- `independent`: Business of Fashion, the BBC, regulators (AFM, BIPT) and AO3.

The first run wrote some reasons in Dutch, copying the Dutch notes from the 20 October list. The prompt now asks for English, and the rerun came back in English. Small trade sites are where the model is least sure: Dieline came back independent once and `interested` once. That is the reason a person can change any rating.

## Checked

- `test/source-perspective.test.mjs`, 12 tests:
  - the levels and the record of who and when;
  - a competitor rated without the model;
  - the prompt and the parser;
  - what is rated and what is left alone;
  - a failed batch, and the limit;
  - the sources list;
  - `discover.mjs perspective` run end to end against a stand-in `claude`;
  - the route through the real server: a team member, the generic patch, a member of gentells.com.
- Mutation check: seven guards undone one at a time, and each turns a test red:
  - admitted sources rated;
  - a competitor sent to the model;
  - a value outside the three accepted;
  - existing ratings redone;
  - the route recording `engine` instead of the person;
  - the patch guard removed;
  - the command not wired.
- Not covered: the scout storing the rating with a new proposal. That path reaches the web, and there is no test of it.
- Full suite, pinned to the tag v0.18.0: 1387 of 1393. The six that fail are `report-render`, which needs `pdftoppm`; it isn't on the workbench, and they fail there without this change too. `tsc` is clean.

## Order

Merge the Standard (v0.18.0, tagged) first, then this, then the dashboard change.
params.title: Every proposed source says whether it has a stake in what it says (Standard 0.18.0)
